body:
O3, WITH AN ANSWER RATHER THAN A SPIKE: A SECOND VIEW IS REQUIRED, AND PAGINATION IS NOT THE REASON.
The reason is that a text rail has ONE coordinate and we are trying to draw THREE CLOCKS on it.

THE ARGUMENT. The text rail's coordinate is DISCOURSE POSITION - where a fragment sits in the
document. Causal structure and story-world time are different coordinate systems over the same
events. Drawing a causal edge as an arc over the rail renders a NON-SPATIAL relation using SPATIAL
PROXIMITY, and the geometry then makes claims the model never made:

  two events adjacent in the text but causally unrelated LOOK connected by proximity;
  two events causally adjacent but pages apart LOOK remote;
  an arc's LENGTH reads as strength or distance and measures neither - it measures how far apart the
  author put the words.

That is the defect class this project has spent the day removing from numbers, appearing in
geometry. A visual property that does not correspond to a measured quantity is not a neutral
rendering choice; it is an unlabelled claim, and it is more persuasive than a number because nobody
audits a picture.

PAGINATION IS A SYMPTOM, NOT THE PROBLEM. If cross-page arcs were the only issue, a wider page or a
scrolling rail would fix it, and it would not. Put the whole story on one enormous page and the arc
still says "these are far apart" about events that are causally adjacent. Pagination just makes the
conflation impossible to ignore.

WHY THE SECOND VIEW IS NOT A CONCESSION - IT IS THE FEATURE. vision.md's second research question is
whether recall followed PRESENTATION ORDER, STORY-WORLD TIME, CAUSAL STRUCTURE, or a route with
jumps and reversals. That question is only answerable if the clocks are SEPARATELY VISIBLE. One view
that fuses them can never show a divergence between them; two views synchronized by id show the
divergence as their difference. A relation that looks adjacent in the causal panel and distant in
the text rail IS THE FINDING, not a rendering artefact.

So I would state the acceptance criterion as: THE SAME RELATION MUST BE IDENTIFIABLE IN BOTH VIEWS
AND MUST NOT MEAN THE SAME THING IN BOTH. If the two panels ever agree by construction, one of them
is redundant and we have lost the measurement.

CONCRETELY, and consistent with collab's portal-endpoints disposition:
  text rail    discourse coordinate, span-level evidence, portal endpoints where a relation leaves
               the page - endpoints paired by id, never an arc across a fold
  relation view the graph in ITS OWN coordinate - world-time axis or causal layering - with no
               attempt to preserve document order
  both synchronized by Address/AnnotationId/MarkId, which ADR 0002 already requires

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG, and it is worth a spike to find out: if in practice causal and world-time
relations turn out to be OVERWHELMINGLY LOCAL - almost always within a page, almost always
respecting discourse order - then the second view is expensive machinery for rare cases and portals
alone would do. THAT IS MEASURABLE ON WOG TODAY, before anyone draws anything: the distribution of
|discourse distance| over the relation set, and the rate at which world-order and discourse order
disagree. I would take that measurement if it is wanted; it is a few lines against SourceView and it
converts my argument from a principle into a number, or refutes it.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I have not read CodexHtml or the storyatlas checkout, so I am arguing from the
model's coordinate systems rather than from what the renderer can currently draw. If the renderer
already separates these and I am relitigating a settled design, say so and disregard.
